Interactive Map of Council Control

    How to use this map
    1. Default view: the map shows which party, if any, holds majority control of each municipality. Grey municipalities are hung. Use the 2021 and 2026 buttons to switch between the two elections.
    2. Find your area: type a municipality’s name or pick it from the list, or zoom (scroll, pinch, or the + and − buttons) and drag the map.
    3. Hover over a council (tap it on a phone) to see its seats, votes, and turnout in 2021 and 2026. Click it to keep the panel open; click it again, or press Esc, to close it.
    4. Reading the figures: each dot is a seat, with the largest party on the left. A party whose dots reach past the dashed line from the left holds a majority. If no party reaches the dashed line, the council is hung.
    Variable definitions
    • Majority: a party holds more than half the council’s seats. Hung: no party does. Control is as the Electoral Commission reports it; who governs a hung council (coalitions, mayors) is not shown.
    • Seats are ward and PR seats together. Ward councillors elected as independents are shown together as Independents.
    • Vote shares are of valid votes on the council’s proportional representation (PR) ballot. Seats are allocated on ward and PR votes together.
    • Turnout: PR ballots cast (valid and spoilt) as a share of registered voters, each year on its own voters’ roll.
    • Some municipalities’ boundaries changed between 2021 and 2026; where 1% or more of voters moved, the council’s panel says so (estimated with the 2011 census population).
    • 2026 results are provisional: downloaded before the Electoral Commission certified them.
    Data: Electoral Commission of South Africa (election returns and council seats), Municipal Demarcation Board (boundaries), and Statistics South Africa (2011 census).
